events.title: The Third Lateran Council
events.shortBlurb: Alexander III gathered the Church at the Lateran to repair the schism — and fixed the two-thirds rule by which popes are chosen still…
body: Fresh from the Peace of Venice, which in 1177 had ended his eighteen-year schism with Frederick Barbarossa and a line of antipopes, Alexander III summoned the Church to the Lateran. The council opened on 5 March 1179, as Archbishop William of Tyre, our chief witness, records, with some three hundred bishops and a great body of abbots gathered about the pope.

In three sessions the fathers issued twenty-seven canons. The first reserved papal elections to the cardinals alone and required a two-thirds majority — the rule by which conclaves have been governed ever since. Others condemned the Cathar heretics of southern France and the mercenary bands then ravaging Christendom, forbade Jews and Muslims to keep Christian servants, and charged every cathedral church to maintain a schoolmaster for poor scholars.

Reckoned the eleventh ecumenical council, the Third Lateran repaired the wreckage of the schism and set the legal frame of the medieval papacy on firmer ground; thirty-six years later Innocent III would build upon it at the Fourth.
